newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volvo trucks Jan-Aug sales down 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volvo trucks Jan-Aug sales down 17 pct.

text.p: Swedish truck maker AB Volvo said on Thursday that total deliveries for the first eight months of 1996 were down 17 percent to 41,900 units.

Tommy Rengman, executive vice president of Volvo Trucks, said in the text of a speech for the IAA truck exhibition that the drop in sales was due substantially to slower sales in North and South American markets.
"The total markets there have declined dramatically," Rengman said.

But Rengman said Volvo's truck deliveries to European markets were up seven percent during the period from January to August and now takes second place in European sales statistics with a 16.2 percent market share.

In the North American market, sales were down 38 percent to 11,681 units from 18,936 units in the year-ago period, while South American sales were down 44 percent to 3,202 units from 5,751 units in the year-ago period.
Rengman said in a briefing to reporters that he expected a turnaround in the American markets.
In Europe, Volvo said invoice units during the January to August period were up seven percent to 22,980 units, but sales in other markets were down 10 percent to 4,025 units.
